title: Applied ML evals: integrated playbook for eval harness, prompt sets, onboarding, guardrails, quantization, and regression triage
author: Elena Park
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood's standards and operational playbooks for applied ML evaluations: the eval-harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profiling guidance, and the regression triage process. It is intended as the canonical cross-functional reference for ML engineers, research engineers, platform owners, and SREs responsible for model rollout and quality monitoring.

Goals:
- Provide a single, actionable playbook that reduces time-to-onboard new models into production.
- Define test coverage (functional, safety, perf), acceptance thresholds, and escalation paths for regressions.
- Standardize prompt set construction and benchmark hygiene so evaluations are reproducible and auditable.
- Document quantization profile creation and verification to minimize degradation risks.

Scope:
Covers model onboarding for text generation and embedding models used by the Redwood API and Dedicated runtime. Does NOT cover private-deploy-only operational steps (see /eng-private-deployments for deployment-specific controls).

Owners and contacts:
- Document owner: Elena Park (Applied ML)
- Primary owners: Applied ML team (onboarding & evals), Runtime QA (performance), Eng-SRE (production monitoring)
- Emergency contact: oncall-eng-sre@redwood.internal

High-level process overview:
1) Pre-onboarding: gather model metadata, training provenance, license and security review.
2) Local eval harness runs: unit tests, prompt-set benchmarks, safety classifiers, and quantization smoke tests.
3) Integration: run end-to-end service-level evals on a staging instance with production-like traffic patterns.
4) Canary rollout + monitoring: gradual traffic ramp with quality gates and automated rollback.
5) Post-rollout: continued sampling, scheduled regression scans, and periodic re-evaluation after infra or model changes.

Standards and acceptance criteria
- Functional correctness: targeted prompt-set pass rate >= 95% for core use-cases.
- Safety: no high-confidence safety violations on curated adversarial lists; any single critical violation fails onboarding.
- Latency: p99 request latency must be within the model tier SLO (see table below).
- Cost: expected per-token cost within 20% of comparable reference model unless approved by Product.

SLO/threshold reference table:
| Metric | Target (Tiered) | Owner | Notes |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| P95 latency (inference) | < 120ms (low), < 250ms (medium), < 500ms (high) | Eng-Serving-Runtime | Measured on 512-token workloads |
| P99 latency | < 250ms (low), < 500ms (medium), < 1s (high) | Eng-Serving-Runtime | Tail latency under typical batching |
| Functional pass-rate | >= 95% | Applied ML | Per prompt-set and aggregate |
| Safety violations (critical) | 0 tolerated | Security & Applied ML | Blocker for onboarding |

Eval harness standards (how to run, required outputs)
- Required artifacts for every model candidate: model-card.json, weights provenance, license.txt, sample inference script, and an evaluation report (pdf or markdown).
- Eval harness runs (automated):
  - Unit tests: tokenization, strange inputs, deterministic seeds where applicable.
  - Prompt-set benchmarks: run full prompt catalog; collect token counts, generation times, pass/fail per test.
  - Safety scan: run standard safety classifers and adversarial lists (see prompt-sets/safety-adversarial catalog).
  - Perf benchmark: throughput (tokens/sec), steady-state latency, and memory/KV cache behaviors.
- Output: standardized eval_report.json and a artifacts tarball uploaded to artifact storage with path pattern: s3://redwood-evals/{model_name}/{sha}/.

Prompt sets and benchmarks (construction & hygiene)
- Prompt set taxonomy:
  - Core functional: representative customer prompts across product verticals.
  - Edge cases: intentionally adversarial or malformed prompts.
  - Safety and content: harmful content tests and PII extraction tests.
  - Latency/throughput: long-context prompts, multi-turn sessions.
- Prompt metadata fields (required): id, intent, expected_outputs (one or more), difficulty, tags, source_owner, created_at.
- Reproducibility: each prompt must be runnable as a single JSON test case in the eval harness and include random-seed where nondeterministic evaluation is expected.
- Benchmark versioning: prompt-sets are versioned with semantic versioning (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Changes that modify expected outputs require a minor version bump.

Model onboarding checklist (step-by-step)
1. Intake form completed with model_name, version, sha, training_data_summary, license, sensitive-data-flag.
2. Security & license review (Security team sign-off).
3. Run eval harness: unit tests, prompt-set benchmarks, safety scans, perf tests.
4. Run quantization profiles (if applicable): draft INT8/4-bit profile under controlled environment.
5. Staging integration: deploy to staging cluster; run E2E traffic replay for 24 hours.
6. Canary: 1% traffic for 4 hours -> quality gates -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% following successful checks.
7. Post-deploy audit: ingest sampling logs, human review of a 100-sample set, and schedule 30/90-day re-eval.

Quality guardrails and monitoring
- Continuous evaluation: nightly runs of core prompt-sets against production model variants and a weekly regression suite.
- Automated alerts: triggered when functional pass-rate drops > 3 percentage points or when p99 latency increases > 30% from baseline.
- Alert routing: PagerDuty for severity P0/P1 regressions; Slack #ml-quality for P2 incidents.
- Human-in-the-loop review: policy requires a cross-functional triage within 24 hours for any P0/P1.

Quantization profiles (guidance and verification)
- Objective: reduce memory and CPU/GPU compute without introducing unacceptable quality regressions.
- Standard profiles: per-layer symmetric/asymmetric, per-channel scaling, and KV-cache-aware sharding.
- Recommended workflow:
  1. Generate FP16 baseline metrics on representative prompt sets.
  2. Run candidate quantization (INT8 or 4-bit) with calibration dataset drawn from real prompts (~10k tokens).
  3. Measure delta on functional pass-rate, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and safety classifiers. Threshold: functional pass-rate drop <= 1.5% for non-critical tasks; <= 0.5% for critical tasks.
  4. If regression exceeds thresholds, iterate with higher precision for specific layers or use mixed-precision profile.
- Artifacts: quant_profile.yaml, quant_report.json, and model build tag uploaded alongside eval artifacts.

Regression triage playbook (when an eval detects a regression)
1. Automated detection: nightly/regression pipelines flag failing prompt-tests or metric drifts.
2. Initial triage (within 4 hours): Applied ML identifies whether regression is due to model change, infra change, prompt drift, or data skew.
3. Priority assignment:
   - P0: critical customer-facing regression (safety or severe functional loss). Immediate rollback + incident declared.
   - P1: significant degradation requiring hotfix or rollback within 24 hours.
   - P2: degraded but acceptable; scheduled fix in next sprint.
4. Rollback criteria: any P0 or safety-critical P1 requires automated rollback to last known-good model.
5. Root cause analysis: full RCA to be completed within 7 days, with action items and owner assignment.

Runbook: step-by-step for a detected nightly regression
1. Confirm alert in the regression dashboard and reproduce locally with failing prompt IDs.
2. Check recent model deployments and infra changes in the last 72 hours.
3. If model change suspected, run previous-model eval artifacts to verify baseline divergence.
4. If infra suspected (e.g., quantization runtime change), re-run model with FP16 runtime and compare.
5. Communicate: post summary to #ml-quality and notify customer success for affected customers.
6. If rollback triggered, follow the Canary rollback checklist and monitor metrics for 2 hours post-rollback.

Operational dashboards and artifacts
- Required dashboards: nightly-regression, model-comparison, prompt-failure-explorer, quantization-regressions.
- Artifact retention: eval artifacts retained for 365 days; model binaries retained per contract.

Appendix: Example eval command and minimal JSON outputs
- Quick eval command (example):
  make eval MODEL_NAME=example-model SHA=abcdef123 ARTIFACT_BUCKET=s3://redwood-evals/example-model/abcdef123
- Minimal eval_report.json keys expected:
  - model_name
  - sha
  - date
  - prompt_set_version
  - functional_pass_rate
  - safety_violations_count
  - latency_p95
  - latency_p99
  - artifacts_path
